question: Anshuman and Kunal together invested ₹36,400 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹19,500, Kunal's share was ₹6,300. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When investment time is constant, Investment Ratio = Profit Ratio.

Total profit = ₹19,500 | Kunal's profit = ₹6,300 | Anshuman's profit = ₹13,200

Difference in profit = 13200 − 6300 = ₹6,900

Investment difference = Total Investment × (Profit Difference ÷ Total Profit)

Investment difference = 36400 × (6900 ÷ 19500) = 36400 × (23 ÷ 65) = ₹12,880

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,880.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total investment = ₹36,400

Total profit = ₹19,500

Kunal's profit share = ₹6,300

**Formula Used:**

In a partnership where the time period is equal, the ratio of investments is exactly equal to the ratio of their profits.

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total Investment = ₹36,400
 
 Anshuman (44 parts)
 
 Kunal (21 parts)
 

 Difference = 23 parts (₹12,880)
 Profit Ratio = ₹13,200 : ₹6,300 = 44 : 21

**Calculations:**

⇒ Anshuman's profit = Total Profit − Kunal's profit

⇒ Anshuman's profit = 19500 − 6300 = ₹13,200

⇒ Profit Ratio (Anshuman : Kunal) = 13200 : 6300 = 132 : 63 = 44 : 21

⇒ Since their investment time duration is the same, Investment Ratio = 44 : 21

⇒ Let Anshuman's investment be 44x and Kunal's be 21x.

⇒ Total investment = 44x + 21x = 65x

⇒ 65x = 36400

⇒ x = 36400 ÷ 65 = 560

⇒ Difference in their investments = 44x − 21x = 23x

⇒ Difference = 23 × 560 = ₹12,880

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,880.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When partners invest their capital for the same time period, the profit or loss is distributed purely in the ratio of their invested capitals. Profit Ratio = C₁ : C₂

Compound Partnership

If capitals are invested for different time durations, the equivalent capital is calculated as Capital × Time. The profit is distributed as C₁×T₁ : C₂×T₂.

Working vs Sleeping Partner

A working partner manages the business and receives a fixed salary or a certain percentage of the profit before the remaining profit is divided. A sleeping partner only invests capital and receives profit according to their investment ratio.
